newsitem.title: MONACO: INTERVIEW - M&G Re chief to oversee Swiss Re merger.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - M&G Re chief to oversee Swiss Re merger.

text.p: John Engestrom, chief executive of UK reinsurer Mercantile & General Re, says he will stay with the company to oversee its amalgamation with its new parent, Swiss Re.
"I am committed to being part of the implementation of the takeover," he told Reuters at a reinsurance conference in Monte Carlo.
"Beyond that, I am in talks with Swiss Re about how best to use my expertise," he said.
Engestrom said he expected restructuring after last month's 1.75 billion stg takeover of M&G Re by the Swiss reinsurance giant to last until the middle of next year.

"Restructuring is a long haul process, it will not happen over the next few months. We expect to set up joint working parties soon, but plans will not be announced until after regulatory approval in November or December," he said.
Swiss Re, now the world's largest life reinsurer, has already announced that it will move control of its life and health operations from Zurich to London.

Engestrom said he was glad that the company had been bought by a committed long-term owner, and that he was not worried about the prospect of losing the independence M&G Re had under previous owner Prudential Corp Plc.
"Independence is not the value driver, it is innovation to the market. Independence of thought is more important than independence of ownership," he said.
Engestrom said he thought the reinsurance market has seen the last of the major acquisitions this year, although he accepted that there may still be some moves among smaller players.
However, he said it was difficult to predict what effect the summer of consolidation would have on the reinsurance market, where most expect rates to soften in the forthcoming renewal season.
Some practitioners have suggested that rates might be stiffened by having a greater proportion of capital in the hands of fewer, stronger players.

But as Engestrom pointed out: "If companies want their return on equity to go up they have to write profitable business, but first they have to write more business. In doing so something has to give out, and that means ratings."
He also accepted that despite regular pleas to the industry to say no to heavily discounted ratings, the reinsurance industry has not always been good at learning from the past.
On Tuesday Engestrom will chair the major debate at the conference on whether international financial markets will replace traditional reinsurance. He believes the two elements can work in tandem.
"Capital market solutions will be a feature of big risk solutions of the future, there is no doubt about that," he said.

"It is needed for cover in areas where reinsurance cannot provide on its own, such as the California Earthquake Authority which was given the green light last week. That is a good hybrid solution to a complex problem," he said.
